project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 271 (System produces M revisions of the exploration policy source between iterations, which returns candidate modules)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 271 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the first act of docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §C5's dreaming loop and the first clause of docs §12.1's middle rung — *"run `M` code revisions of `π`"*, the production of the candidate set the sweep evaluates. Two halves in one new pure module, dreaming/reviser.py. (1) The value — a candidate module, :class:`CandidateModule`: the revised policy **source** (a complete Python module the replay engine can import as a policy), its ``code_hash`` (sha256 of the source — the identity feature 274 persists to ``policy_revision.code_hash``, migration ``0109``), its ``module_id`` (a version string derived from the code_hash, collision-free for distinct sources, the spelling the loop hands to feature 274 as ``policy_version``), its ``parent_version`` (the incumbent it was derived from — ``π^0 = π_t``, nullable for a root) and its ``revision_index`` (1..M). Frozen, __slots__, validated at construction, the member's FreezeRecord/CapRecord precedent. (2) The act — :func:`revise_policy(incumbent_source, count, *, seed=…, incumbent_version=None, reviser=None)`: validates the ask, then produces ``count`` candidate modules, one per revision index 1..M, each a **structure-preserving** transform of the incumbent's authored source — the AST's identifiers, control flow and call structure are unchanged and only the numeric-literal *values* are jittered by a deterministic, seeded, bounded factor — and returns them in index order. The transform is admissible **by construction**: because it changes magnitudes and adds no comparison, no hardcoded node id, no unreachable path and no model call, a candidate descended from an admitted incumbent still carries none of feature 230's four anti-patterns nor feature 231's learned component — so the candidates are exactly the kind feature 230 admits, and the loop screens each with policy-runtime's ``screen_policy`` before replay (feature 271 owns production, feature 230 owns the gate, and this member imports no other member). The default reviser is that seeded numeric jitter (:func:`default_reviser`, the REVISION_BAND default the loop's offline tuning replaces, exactly the way feature 227's ``_PATIENCE_FLOOR`` and feature 277's schedule state a named default the cycle supersedes); a pluggable ``reviser`` lets a deployment substitute its own ``(incumbent_source, revision_index, seed) -> source`` policy-development strategy without moving the contract. The production is **deterministic**: the same ``(incumbent_source, count, seed, incumbent_version)`` answers the same candidate modules to the last code_hash in any process — docs §12's determinism contract, the same property feature 278's split and feature 279's rotation hold one transform over. ``revise_policy`` deduplicates the produced candidates by ``code_hash`` and **refuses** with :class:`RevisionError` when it cannot produce ``count`` *distinct* candidates — a policy with too few authored constants to perturb names no sweep of ``M`` — rather than silently returning duplicates that would collapse the argmax onto one source. It is **pure**: no store, no pool read, no clock, no environment, no ``@register`` component — it reads the incumbent source the caller already holds and opens no database, the same read-side stance feature 230 takes for its own gate. Two new error siblings under DreamingError: :class:`RevisionRequestError` (the ask's own facts — malformed incumbent source, count, seed or parent version, refused before anything is produced) and :class:`RevisionError` (the production verdict — a revised source that does not parse, or a shortfall of distinct candidates). No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no table is created (the module persists nothing — feature 274 writes the argmax into ``policy_revision``); the member's single "dreaming" component is untouched and the seat is not edited — feature 275's floor names set that precedent and feature 271 follows it. The module joins by workspace-scan convention and imports no other workspace member; stdlib only — ``ast``, ``hashlib`` and ``secrets``/``hashlib`` for the deterministic draw.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/ <member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/dreaming/tests/`). Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The dreaming member is stdlib-only, and feature 271 keeps it that way: ast, hashlib.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, hand-written __slots__ value classes for store records (the member's FreezeRecord precedent), docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition, member-owned tables created lazily beside the only module that writes them (never in the shared migration chain, which is order-sensitive and excluded from this feature's file claim), per-occurrence row ids so a retried window never collides on the primary key, the §12 ordering rule (ordered history reads), and the error-vocabulary discipline that no member imports another and a caller must be able to catch one feature's refusal without catching a neighbouring feature's (translate at the seam). Features 270 (the cycle freeze, cycle.py), 275 (the ladder floor, ladder.py), 277 (the revision cap, cap.py), 276 (the 20–50 ceiling, ceiling.py), 278 (the split, split.py), 279 (the rotation, rotation.py), 280 (the selection bar, bar.py), 281 (the paired comparison, paired.py), 282 (the family transfer, transfer.py) already live in this member; feature 271 is a new sentence within it — the *production* half of the sweep, pure and store-free, the read-side sibling of feature 230's gate. Features 272 (evaluate each candidate on every stored world), 273 (keep the incumbent in the candidate set) and 274 (persist the argmax to policy_revision) are parallel siblings and MUST NOT be imported or assumed present — feature 271 produces the candidates those consume and does none of their acts.

category.name: Dreaming Loop & Meta-Selection
category.feature: System produces M revisions of the exploration policy source between iterations, which returns candidate modules.

project_specification.integration_points: Feature 271 is the production half of the §C5 sweep and the first of the 271-274 chain the dreaming member's own docstring names as "depending on this one" (feature 270): the M-revision sweep runs inside the outer iteration whose pool feature 270 holds fixed, so ``depends_on="270"`` is the loop-ordering fact, **not** a code import — revise_policy is pure and imports nothing from dreaming.cycle, the way the member's no-cross-member rule requires. The candidates it returns are consumed by the three siblings that follow: feature 272 replays each candidate module's source against every stored world (reading the source this module returns, not a path or a checkpoint), feature 273 adds the incumbent (π^0, the parent_version this module records) back into the candidate set so the argmax never falls below the current policy, and feature 274 aggregates each candidate over the pool and persists the argmax — writing the winner's module_id as policy_revision.policy_version and its code_hash as policy_revision.code_hash (migration 0109). Feature 271 persists nothing itself: a candidate module is a value the sweep carries, and only the selected one becomes a row. The count M the loop runs is feature 277's schedule (dreaming.cap.revision_cap) and is bounded before the sweep by feature 276's ceiling (dreaming.ceiling.rejects_uncapped_sweep) — feature 271 takes the count it is handed and does not re-decide it, the same "judgment over a count the caller already has" split the cap, the ceiling, the floor and the split all take. Each produced candidate is screened by the loop with policy-runtime's screen_policy (feature 230, the admission gate in the policy-runtime member) before replay: feature 271 produces candidates admissible by construction and feature 230 pronounces admissibility, two acts across two members that this feature never joins — the candidate's source is the only thing that crosses the boundary, and a candidate that fails the gate is the loop's to discard, not this module's to pre-refuse. The seed that fixes the jitter is the cycle's own act — the loop passes a cycle-derived seed (the iteration id, the way feature 279's rotation keys its split on the cycle's name), so a retried sweep at the same seed reproduces the same candidates the way feature 279 reproduces the same holdout. The module is reached directly from the member (`from dreaming import revise_policy, default_reviser, candidate_module, CandidateModule, RevisionRequestError, RevisionError, REVISION_BAND`) and re-exported by the member __init__, the way feature 275's floor names are.
project_specification.constraints: - The candidate module is exactly five facts and nothing derived at construction beyond its identity: ``source`` (non-empty text — a blank or non-str source is refused), ``code_hash`` (sha256 hex of the source, computed by the factory, never handed in), ``module_id`` (derived from the code_hash, non-empty, collision-free for distinct sources — the factory defaults it to a ``cand-``-prefixed code_hash digest when the caller names none), ``parent_version`` (None or non-empty text; None for a root, the incumbent's version otherwise) and ``revision_index`` (a genuine positive integer — a bool is not an index). The value is frozen with hand-written __slots__, the member's FreezeRecord stance, so two callers holding one candidate cannot move each other's source. - The revision is **structure-preserving**: the default reviser parses the incumbent with ``ast``, jitters only numeric-literal *values* by a deterministic bounded factor in ``[1 − REVISION_BAND, 1 + REVISION_BAND]`` derived per literal-site from ``(seed, revision_index)`` via hashlib (no ``random`` — the draw must reproduce across processes), and unparses with ``ast.unparse``. It changes no identifier, no control-flow node, no call, no import and no comparison, so a candidate descended from an admitted incumbent carries none of feature 230's four anti-patterns (no absolute score constant, no hardcoded node id, ``commit()`` reachable on every terminating path) and none of feature 231's learned component — the transform alters a magnitude where those checks look at structure. A zero constant is jittered additively so it is not annihilated; a bool literal is left untouched (it is not a tunable magnitude). The jitter factor is a pure function of ``(seed, revision_index, site)`` so the same inputs reproduce the same candidate in any process (docs §12). - The production is deterministic and pure: revise_policy reads the incumbent source the caller already holds and opens no database, reads no pool row, resolves no path, imports nothing that could (no sqlite3, no os, no environment). ``depends_on="270"`` is the loop-ordering fact, not a code dependency — the module imports nothing from dreaming.cycle. - The count is taken, not decided: revise_policy accepts the ``count`` it is handed (a genuine positive integer — zero, a negative, a bool, a float or a non-str/non-int is refused with RevisionRequestError) and produces one candidate per index 1..count. It does not cap the count (feature 276's ceiling refuses a too-wide sweep *before* the loop calls this) and does not read the pool to size it (feature 275's floor is the loop's precondition, checked before the sweep — a pool too thin to dream on is refused before revise_policy is ever called, so this module does not mint a thin-pool refusal and does not import ladder.py). - Distinctness is a verdict, not a silence: revise_policy deduplicates the produced candidates by code_hash and, if fewer than ``count`` distinct candidates remain, refuses with RevisionError naming the shortfall — a policy whose authored constants cannot fund ``M`` distinct perturbations names no sweep of that size, and returning duplicates would collapse the argmax onto one source. The default reviser therefore requires an incumbent carrying perturbable numeric constants; a source with none is the shortfall's common case and is refused, not padded. - Two new error siblings under DreamingError — RevisionRequestError (the ask: malformed incumbent source, count, seed or parent version, refused before anything is produced) and RevisionError (the verdict: a revised source that does not parse, or a shortfall of distinct candidates) — that borrow none of the member's existing classes and are borrowed by none of them. Neither carries a code word: feature 271's verb is *produces*, so every refusal opens with its subject (the shape features 276, 278 and 282's code-word-free sentences state), and the production verdict is a developer fact the loop repairs by growing the policy's authored constants or shrinking M, not an operator-greppable selection outcome like feature 280's bar. - Feature 271 produces candidates; it does **not** evaluate, select, keep the incumbent, or persist. It never runs a policy, never scores a world, never reads replay_score or bootstrap_world, never writes a policy_revision row, and never includes π^0 in its own output — those are features 272, 273 and 274, parallel siblings that consume this module's candidates and MUST NOT be imported or assumed present. The admissibility gate (feature 230) is the loop's verb over the produced source, not this module's; feature 271 states that its candidates are admissible by construction and names the gate, but imports neither policy_runtime nor its screen. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited. No new @register component, no table, no persistence, and no seat export: feature 270's single "dreaming" component is the member's whole composition and its suite (test_component.py) is untouched. The module is re-exported from the member __init__ and its docstring carries the new sentence, the way feature 275's floor names are. - All existing tests in the dreaming member (packages/dreaming/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the value and the vocabulary. Add RevisionRequestError and RevisionError to dreaming.errors as siblings of the member's existing classes under DreamingError, following the repair-split discipline (the request refusal is *the ask was malformed — re-consider the source, count or seed*; the verdict refusal is *the policy cannot fund M distinct revisions — grow its authored constants or shrink M*; neither is the thin pool's *grow the pool*, the freeze's *wait*, or the bar's *keep the incumbent*), and extend the errors module docstring with the sweep's production sentence. Add dreaming/reviser.py with REVISION_BAND (the jitter half-width, a named default the loop's offline tuning replaces), the CandidateModule value class (hand-written __slots__, the five facts, validated at construction — source non-empty text, revision_index a genuine positive non-bool int, parent_version None or non-empty text, code_hash and module_id non-empty), and the candidate_module(source, *, parent_version=None, revision_index=1, module_id=None) factory that computes code_hash = sha256(source), defaults module_id to a cand-prefixed digest, validates and returns the value — the one spelling of a candidate, so the sweep and any later feature in this category build one through it.

Phase 2 — the act. In dreaming/reviser.py add default_reviser (incumbent_source, revision_index, seed) — parse with ast, jitter only numeric-literal values by the deterministic bounded factor derived per site from (seed, revision_index) via hashlib, leave bools and structure untouched, unparse and return the source — and revise_policy(incumbent_source, count, *, seed=…, incumbent_version=None, reviser=None): validate the ask (RevisionRequestError for a blank or non-str incumbent, a non-positive/non-int/bool count, a malformed seed, or a malformed parent version, each naming what it refused), run the pluggable reviser (default_reviser when none is given) once per index 1..count, build each candidate through candidate_module with the passed incumbent_version as parent_version, deduplicate by code_hash, refuse with RevisionError on a shortfall of distinct candidates, and return the tuple in index order. Re-export everything from the member __init__ and extend the member docstring with the production sentence. The seed is validated as text or int and drives only the deterministic draw — it is never stored, and the same seed reproduces the same candidates.

Phase 3 — the tests and verification. Add packages/dreaming/tests/ test_reviser.py pinning: the value contract (a blank/non-str source refused, a bool revision_index refused, a negative index refused, a root parent_version None, the code_hash equals sha256(source), the module_id default derives from the code_hash and a caller-named one is honoured, two equal sources answer equal frozen values), the determinism law (the same (incumbent, count, seed) answers the same code_hashes in a second process-order, and count candidates at indices 1..count), the structure-preserving transform (ast.dump of a candidate matches the incumbent modulo numeric-constant values; identifiers, control flow and calls unchanged; a bool literal untouched; a zero constant jittered additively not annihilated), the distinctness verdict (a policy with several authored thresholds yields count distinct candidates; a source with no perturbable constant refuses with RevisionError naming the shortfall, leaving nothing produced), the count validation (0, −1, a bool, a float, a non-str each refused with RevisionRequestError), the seed and parent-version validation, the pluggable-reviser seam (a custom reviser's sources flow through unchanged and a reviser that returns the incumbent verbatim collapses to the shortfall refusal), the pure-function shape verified by denial (no sqlite3 / os / open / environment access on the module), and the vocabulary siblinghood (the request/verdict split, no code word, opens with the subject). Extend test_errors.py with the reviser pair's sibling test. Run the member suite (uv run pytest packages/dreaming/tests) and the repository-level suite (uv run pytest tests/) — both — and lint only the changed files against a sibling.
